content.comment_body: Hello, I downloaded the app to my Samsung Galaxy S3, and it functions on my local network (LAN). However, when I attempt to connect to my [product_name] device over the internet (WAN), an error appears: "Can't connect to device, please check connection." Here's what I did: - Entered my external IP in the app's IP-address field - Forwarded port 10001 to the internal IP address of the [product_name] (it's connected to my router) - Tried disabling the router firewall, which did not resolve the issue Reviewing the router log, I notice external connection attempts forwarded to port 10001. I also monitored the firmware version check on my [product_name]; the Rx/Tx lights flash briefly, so it seems there's a connection attempt. However, the connection doesn't establish. If I connect over Wi-Fi directly to the internal IP, the app works perfectly. What steps can I take to enable access via the internet? Is there anything specific I should check? Additional Info (August 6, 2013): I forwarded port 10001 to my PC instead of the [product_name] to monitor the traffic with Wireshark. Attached is the Wireshark output. I tested connections both through LAN and WAN and notice no real differences—the data reaches my PC correctly and the router doesn't appear to be blocking traffic. But connection to the [product_name] still fails. I did notice the Tx/Rx LED behaviour differs: over LAN, it flashes quickly and repeatedly; over WAN, only a few slow flashes appear. There is some traffic, but something goes wrong. Assistance appreciated!

I managed to resolve the issue by routing the traffic through my PC before directing it to the [product_name]. For details, see [url]. However, I'm still unsure why port forwarding directly to the [product_name] doesn't work, while forwarding it through my PC does. If anyone can clarify, I'd appreciate it. Thanks, [user_name]
This thread is closed because the question has already been addressed in another post regarding connecting with [product_name] [article_no] over the internet. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: A user encountered issues accessing their [product_name] remotely over the internet. Although direct local connections worked without problems, forwarding ports to the device for remote access was unsuccessful until the user routed the traffic through a PC first. The underlying reasons are unclear, possibly involving undocumented router settings or limitations of the [product_name] itself.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wishes to control and access the [product_name] device remotely over the internet, expecting it to work as seamlessly as on their local network, simply by forwarding the necessary port to the device without additional hardware.
